races.name: British EBF Restricted Novice Stakes (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Terryfying
runners_data.comment: A 1,000-guinea Dream Ahead gelding whose half-sibling showed limited ability at sprint distances; he faces a tough debut assignment and the pedigree holds little encouragement at this level, making him difficult to recommend without evidence of his own potential.

runners_data.name: Desert Outlaw
runners_data.comment: An Arizona gelding who is a full brother to Glyndwr, who showed useful form at this trip, and his dam also had ability at sprint distances as a two-year-old; he was inexpensively purchased and the assessment is that debut day presents a tough introduction.

runners_data.name: Loveulongtime
runners_data.comment: Overraced on debut at Wetherby and failed to see out the distance, going well beaten; the drop to six furlongs today is a logical step and her trainer is in good form, though she'll need to settle better to show what she's capable of.

runners_data.name: Whisper Angel
runners_data.comment: A 32,000-euro Kodi Bear filly whose half-sister Feyha showed fair ability at twelve furlongs; that staying pedigree is at odds with today's sprint trip, the trainer has been misfiring of late, and facing experienced rivals on debut makes this a tough introduction.

runners_data.name: Location Location
runners_data.comment: Held his early level with a third at Hamilton on his latest start, confirming he's capable at this grade; wears a hood and has tended to race keenly, and while he handles the trip, he has yet to get his head in front in recent starts.

runners_data.name: Market Equities
runners_data.comment: A Bungle Inthejungle colt who is a half-brother to Third Time Lucky, a smart performer at middle distances; no debut form to assess, but he merits respect on pedigree if the market speaks in his favour, though he's ranked in the lower half of our figures.

runners_data.name: Mr Resdev
runners_data.comment: A 30,000-guinea Ardad colt whose half-brother Diligent Resdev showed useful form at six furlongs; he's unraced and not the most obvious proposition for this debut, though that sibling's ability at this trip at least gives him a relevant benchmark.

runners_data.name: Neverbeatdeswalker
runners_data.comment: Demonstrated some flickers of ability on debut at York eighteen days ago while clearly needing the experience; he finished seventh and well beaten, and significant progress is required before he can be seriously considered — he sits at the foot of our figures here.

runners_data.name: Possessive
runners_data.comment: Took the spoils on debut before finding a stiffer test at Epsom too demanding last time, tending to race keenly and finishing well beaten; dropping back into a more suitable grade today is the logical step, and he handles this trip on today's ground, giving him every chance to re-establish himself.

runners_data.name: Kodiak Breeze
runners_data.comment: Made real strides from his debut to take a maiden with authority by over three lengths last time, and he handles today's trip and going; carries a penalty but the form looks solid and he merits genuine respect, with the caveat that his trainer's recent numbers have been quiet.

runners_data.name: Court Legend
runners_data.comment: Well beaten on debut at York, never able to land a blow after being held up early and going down by nine lengths in a seller; significant progress is needed to play a role in this company, though he has only the one outing on his CV.

runners_data.name: Dontlookanyfurther
runners_data.comment: A £35,000 breeze-up purchase by Space Traveller whose dam is a half-sister to a high-class turf sprinter, giving him an intriguing pedigree page for this surface; without a run to assess him, he merits respect on breeding and is placed fourth on our figures.

races.name: British EBF Restricted Novice Stakes (GBB Race) (Div 2)

runners_data.name: That's All Right
runners_data.comment: Ardad colt whose dam was placed over seven and eight furlongs — a modest pedigree profile that makes limited appeal, and the overall picture gives little encouragement for a debut success. Hard to make a case for him in this field.

runners_data.name: Travellers Girl
runners_data.comment: Finished fourth on debut at Ripon, closing ground in the final stages to be beaten three lengths — handled today's distance on good ground and showed ability. She needs to find more to take this but the quality of opposition here looks within her reach.

runners_data.name: Noccalula Falls
runners_data.comment: Soldier's Call filly who is a full sister to a useful performer over a mile — an interesting breeding angle, and the handler is in good current form. Nevertheless, she rates as an outside chance on debut despite those positives.

runners_data.name: Roman Crystal
runners_data.comment: Below-par debut at Ripon, finishing sixth well beaten in a maiden over today's trip — hard to warm to on that evidence. She is open to improvement as a juvenile but a notable step forward is needed to get involved here.

runners_data.name: Scarlet Dynasty
runners_data.comment: Supremacy colt who cost 9,000 euros, a half-brother to a very useful 6f performer — though the dam showed her best form at a much longer trip, creating mixed signals for today's distance. Faces a stiff enough ask on debut.

runners_data.name: Brixworth Bandit
runners_data.comment: Showed clear improvement when fourth at Carlisle latest, beaten six lengths in a novice after a difficult debut, and he handles today's trip on good ground. Connections landed this race last year; he is still searching for his first success but has shown enough to have a live chance here.

runners_data.name: Claret Time
runners_data.comment: Showed flashes of ability on debut at Redcar, beaten nine lengths in a novice, and there is reason to think he can build on that over today's distance on good ground. First-time hood fitted; the trainer's recent strike rate gives some pause.

runners_data.name: Mick's The Boy
runners_data.comment: Showed traces of ability on debut in a seller at York, finishing eighth beaten just over seven lengths, and he acts over today's trip on good ground. Improvement is anticipated and would make him a factor; needs to deliver on that promise to be competitive.

runners_data.name: Arapaho Gold
runners_data.comment: Debut winner at this course, taking a maiden by 2½ lengths while still showing some inexperience — barely needing to be fully extended. A physically imposing type with plenty of scope, he acts on today's trip and ground and looks well capable of further progress off a short break.

runners_data.name: Harry Who
runners_data.comment: Space Blues colt purchased for 22,000 euros, a half-brother to a very smart performer over a mile and a quarter — the dam also excelled at that trip, suggesting stamina on both sides. One to monitor in the market on debut, though there is plenty to find on figures.

runners_data.name: Mangham
runners_data.comment: Beaten well clear of the field in a novice at Carlisle on his sole start, he showed very little on that occasion and is extremely hard to fancy against this group.

runners_data.name: Moral Victory
runners_data.comment: Well beaten on his only start, losing ground from a tardy beginning in a novice at Southwell, he has everything to prove in a more competitive environment here and trails the field markedly on our ratings.

runners_data.name: Fair Isle Sioux
runners_data.comment: Outpaced in a maiden at Carlisle most recently, not seeing out a mile, she trails the field on our figures and has plenty to prove before featuring in the finish here.

runners_data.name: Brouhaha
runners_data.comment: Well held in a maiden at Catterick most recently — a backward step from debut level — he faces a tough task with the trainer in a poor run of form and our figures placing him near the foot of the field.

runners_data.name: Fozzie
runners_data.comment: Fourth at Beverley most recently over a shorter trip than ideal, beaten two lengths without producing his best finish, he has solid form claims at this distance on good ground. His profile over seven to ten furlongs marks him out as a genuine contender, though he needs more.

runners_data.name: Lord d'Or
runners_data.comment: Second at York on his second start, beaten three-quarters of a length in a novice over today's trip, he advanced sharply from his debut and tops our figures in this field. Effective at a mile on good ground, he holds leading claims as the one to beat.

runners_data.name: North Force
runners_data.comment: Well beaten when ridden patiently at Nottingham on his latest start after a spell of solid form, he returns wearing first-time cheekpieces in a bid to sharpen up. Effective at six to seven furlongs on a sound surface, the longer trip here adds a further question mark.

runners_data.name: Prince Of Calypso
runners_data.comment: Third at Nottingham most recently, tried in cheekpieces and beaten five and a quarter lengths in a novice over today's distance, he showed consistent promise across both starts on ground that suits. The trainer's lean recent run is a flag, though he handles the trip and can build on his form.

runners_data.name: Steel Raven
runners_data.comment: Third on debut at Carlisle, beaten four lengths in a novice over nine furlongs on good to soft, he showed enough on his introduction to merit serious consideration here. With a trainer operating in good form and room for improvement, he looks a genuine live player.

runners_data.name: Woheela
runners_data.comment: A Lope De Vega filly on debut, wearing a tongue-tie, she is bred with real purpose — out of a dam who was high-class at a mile as a juvenile and a half-sister to a smart performer from twelve to thirteen furlongs. Widely respected; debut inexperience is the only unknown.

races.name: Army Benevolent Fund Handicap

runners_data.name: Ellie's de Vega
runners_data.note: Hold-up style, 3yo on good-to-firm form over course-relevant 6f; consistent top-four finisher but yet to win, and in a 19-runner field will need an unusually clean passage to replicate those placing efforts.
runners_data.comment: Third at Ayr last time over 7f, running to form despite pulling through the early stages, and second on our figures today; effective at 6-7f on good ground and AW, and first-time cheekpieces could help him settle better, though drawn on the outside of a big field.

runners_data.name: Desert Master
runners_data.note: 5yo hold-up specialist whose best recent efforts came over 5-6f on good, but mapped into midfield in this shape rather than the true backmarker slot he needs — his 0W from 15 similar-going runs underlines the frustration of his style when pace is controlled.
runners_data.comment: Fourth at Wetherby last time, beaten 1½ lengths off a mark 1lb above today's; first-time blinkers added and competitive on the weights, though 6f is at the top of his range and he remains without a win in a lengthy run of starts.

runners_data.name: Bishop's Glory
runners_data.note: Prominent racer from Joey Ramsden's yard, where T14 shows recent winner; has handled Thirsk's straight 6f before and should get a natural position tracking Mrs Trump — only one similar-going placing in 15 is a significant concern.
runners_data.comment: Well beaten in each of his last two outings, including at Wetherby recently when 5 lengths adrift; acts at 5-7f on a sound surface and a first-time visor is tried, but he remains without a win in recent starts and considerably more is needed to feature here.

runners_data.name: Indy's Angel
runners_data.note: Philip Kirby's 4yo is a genuine hold-up horse whose recent form shows a string of mid-to-rear finishes in 6-8f handicaps on good; packed into the midfield by race shape and unlikely to get the ground-making run her style demands in such a large field.
runners_data.comment: Beaten 10 lengths at Beverley in her latest handicap and has been off the pace since late 2025; effective at 5-6f on a sound surface, first-time cheekpieces are tried and she carries a light weight from draw 19, but a return to better form is required.

runners_data.name: Hyrcanian
runners_data.note: Ron Barr's 5yo habitually fades in the closing stages — a trait flagged in the form and backed up by four 8th-or-worse finishes in the last five — and being squeezed out of his natural hold-up position by field size compounds that concern.
runners_data.comment: Struggled badly at Ripon last time after a slow exit from the stalls, beaten over 8 lengths and in poor recent form throughout; her better efforts have all come on all-weather surfaces, so today's turf assignment presents another obstacle — hard to fancy at present.

runners_data.name: The Floors Munky
runners_data.note: 3yo who has raced over longer trips (7-8f) and whose most recent 6f runs have seen him fill the bottom half of the field; naturally a closer, he is already racing below his ideal trip and will need significant improvement to matter here.
runners_data.comment: Out of his depth at 1m at Carlisle most recently when failing to see out the trip; the shorter distance here should suit better, and first-time cheekpieces are applied, but he has not shown enough in recent outings to command confidence at this mark.

runners_data.name: Petes Diamond
runners_data.note: Joey Ramsden's 3yo runs in headgear and has spent most of his career in the bottom half of finishes over 6-7f; a natural hold-up runner who, pushed further into the midfield than ideal, has shown nothing in similar going to suggest a first success here.
runners_data.comment: Well beaten at Wolverhampton last time in a classified race, his better form has come on all-weather surfaces; he carries a light weight here but remains without a win in recent starts and has plenty to prove before he can be expected to feature on turf.

runners_data.name: Mister Sky Blue
runners_data.note: Connor Beasley takes the ride on Gemma Tutty's 4yo, who has placed twice on good-to-soft and twice more on similar ground — a genuine prominent racer who should slot in just behind Mrs Trump and is well positioned to benefit if the pace is controlled.
runners_data.comment: Shaped with real promise last time, going down by less than a length off this identical mark, and heads our ratings for this field; first-time blinkers now applied, he acts at 6f on any ground and looks the one to beat.

runners_data.name: Hurstwood
runners_data.note: Peter Niven's 9yo veteran has placed twice in recent 6f handicaps on good and goes in similar conditions again — but his natural hold-up style is crowded out in this shape, and his age profile suggests he needs everything to fall right.
runners_data.comment: Held up for pace in a handicap at Doncaster last time, beaten 5 lengths, and without a win in his last five starts; acts at 6f on any ground and his handicap mark has been nudging lower, but he needs considerably more to feature here.

runners_data.name: Golden Prosperity
runners_data.note: Tony Coyle & Kaine Wood's 7yo wears a hood and has two wins and four places in similar going, making him arguably the most proven finisher among the closers — but displaced from his natural rear position in a big field, getting the gap in time is his primary obstacle.
runners_data.comment: Fourth last time, beaten 2¼ lengths off this same mark, and first-time cheekpieces are applied today; acts at 5-6f on a sound surface, and while without a win in recent starts, there is scope to build on that latest effort here.

runners_data.name: Thehunnebelllegacy
runners_data.note: Richard & Fahey's 3yo ran just nine days ago, has placed third in similar going and is from one of the busiest yards by recent winners (T14: 5/56) — a hold-up horse who has yet to convert, but trainer form and freshness give him a marginal angle.
runners_data.comment: Failed to produce her best at Catterick last time, well beaten in a handicap, and drawn on the outside of a large field here; she is versatile on ground and effective at 5-7f, but rivals appear to hold the stronger hand on our figures.

runners_data.name: Up The Monk
runners_data.note: Michael Appleby's 4yo wears a visor and returns from a 102-day break — his only win came on Southwell's artificial surface over 6f, and good-to-firm turf at Thirsk represents a very different challenge; the layoff and going are genuine flags.
runners_data.comment: Returning from a 14-week absence and fitted with a first-time visor, he offered little at Southwell last time when below form off a 2lb higher mark; his more worthwhile efforts have come on all-weather surfaces, making this turf assignment an additional question mark.

runners_data.name: Everydaysasaturday
runners_data.note: Declan Carroll's 3yo wears blinkers and has not raced for 43 days; most of his form is on Southwell's tapeta over 5-7f and the switch to good-to-firm turf on the big Thirsk straight is an untested variable that is hard to resolve in his favour.
runners_data.comment: Well beaten at Newcastle last time over a shorter trip, making headway in the closing stages; the step up to today's 6f should suit better, and first-time blinkers are tried, though he remains without a win in recent starts and is drawn on the outside of a large field.

runners_data.name: Stormy Pearl
runners_data.note: David Thompson's 6yo has placed four times in five recent 6f runs on good and boasts a win in similar conditions — she is the pick of the hold-up brigade in terms of raw similar-going returns and wears a hood to maintain focus.
runners_data.comment: Third at Carlisle off this exact mark last time and effective at 5-6f on soft and good; she has a tendency to race up with the pace, first-time cheekpieces are applied, and she lines up on a weight below where she last proved successful — solid claims here.

runners_data.name: Dolly's Delight
runners_data.note: Ivan Furtado's 4yo has a win and two places at 6f on similar surfaces; Jason Hart takes the ride, and the shift from 7f trips to 6f is worth noting as her recent runs have mostly been over longer — she may find the tempo of a controlled 6f suits, though her natural closer style faces the same traffic issues as the rest.
runners_data.comment: Failed to show her best at Carlisle last time, well beaten in a handicap, and without a win in her last five starts; effective at 6-7f and probably acts on any ground, but needs to step forward from what she has been showing recently to feature here.

runners_data.name: Night Emperor
runners_data.note: Joanna Mason, usually associated with northern yards, partners this Tina Jackson 4yo who has shown mid-division finishes over 6f on good; 34 days since last run and a low-profile operation make this a speculative hold-up contender at best.
runners_data.comment: Fourth at Ripon last time, beaten 2½ lengths off a 2lb higher mark, and drops 2lb to this; effective at 6f on good ground and there is something to build on from that recent effort, though he remains without a win in his last five starts.

runners_data.name: Mrs Trump
runners_data.note: Paul Midgley's 6yo is the lone confirmed front-runner and the tactical fulcrum of the race — she can dictate fully uncontested from the gates; her recent form reads as placed fourth last time out and she has shown win ability in similar going, though a STYLE_FIT tag warns against assuming she converts control into victory.
runners_data.comment: She landed this contest 12 months ago and is effective at 5-6f on soft and good to firm, but her last five outings have all been well below that level; trainer results have been modest recently, and she needs something to click to feature here.

runners_data.name: Barmyblade
runners_data.note: Tim Easterby's 4yo is by far the busiest yard in the race (T14: 16/99) and has three wins in 15 similar-going appearances; wears a hood, ran 14 days ago, and showed a second and fourth at 5f — his natural closer style is compromised by midfield placement in this shape, but stable form is the strongest positive angle.
runners_data.comment: Runner-up at Ripon last time despite an awkward exit from the stalls, beaten a length off this identical mark; first-time cheekpieces applied, effective at 5-6f on good to soft, and though without a win in recent starts, there is plenty to build on here.

runners_data.name: Uncle Sam
runners_data.note: Ray Craggs' 4yo has placed twice over 5-6f on similar surfaces and was runner-up just 13 days ago — a genuine late finisher who is being pushed into a midfield slot he would not naturally inhabit in a smaller field, meaning Tom Eaves will need to manufacture a run where ordinarily one would develop organically.
runners_data.comment: Second at Southwell last time in a classified event over 5f, beaten 1¼ lengths, and steps up to today's trip; effective across a range of going and distances, he can go well enough when in the mood, though consistency has not been his strong suit in recent outings.

races.paceDynamic: Mrs Trump is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 19-runner 6f handicap and, crucially, faces no genuine pace rival to pressure her — she can dictate from the gates at a controlled, sustainable tempo on good-to-firm ground at Thirsk. The bulk of the field are natural hold-up horses: Stormy Pearl, Golden Prosperity, Hurstwood, Uncle Sam, Barmyblade and others will all be hunting the same patch of late ground, and with the pace compressed into one setter the finishing straight is likely to be a wall of challengers converging simultaneously. Bishop's Glory and Mister Sky Blue carry prominent profiles and should be able to track Mrs Trump into a handy position, giving them first run on the closers. The field holds more hold-up types than the race shape can accommodate at the rear — Uncle Sam, Hurstwood, Golden Prosperity and Barmyblade are all genuine deep closers who will be squeezed into a congested midfield, unable to secure their natural backmarker berth. This race shape — one controlled pace, lots of late traffic — strongly favours horses who can track the leader from a prominent position and produce a sustained, early-in-the-straight challenge rather than a deep hold-up run through a densely packed field.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Mrs Trump Controls, Prominent Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If Mrs Trump sets a measured, uncontested lead and one of the prominent trackers produces a sustained run from 2f out.
scenarios.body: If Mrs Trump sets a measured, uncontested lead and one of the prominent trackers produces a sustained run from 2f out.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Late Surge From Closers
scenarios.trigger: If Mrs Trump's pace is slow enough to compress the field and a genuine closer gets a clean passage to finish with real momentum.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Front Pair Clear
scenarios.trigger: If Mrs Trump's early control is so complete that she simply runs her rivals off their feet and maintains the lead to the line.
scenarios.body: If Mrs Trump's early control is so complete that she simply runs her rivals off their feet and maintains the lead to the line.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Quickens, Field Splits
scenarios.trigger: If a faster-than-expected gallop is set and the field fractures into separate groups, creating a lottery near the far rail.
scenarios.body: If a faster-than-expected gallop is set and the field fractures into separate groups, creating a lottery near the far rail.

watchPoints.text: Mrs Trump is the only confirmed pace-setter in a 19-runner field — if she misses the break or is baulked in the first furlong, the race loses its shape entirely and becomes a slow-run lottery favouring whoever is handiest.

The large cluster of hold-up horses — Golden Prosperity, Barmyblade, Stormy Pearl, Uncle Sam — will all be hunting the same late ground and risk interfering with each other entering the final furlong; watch the draw and early positioning for who gets first run.

Up The Monk returns from a 102-day absence and represents a genuine each-way danger if Appleby has him fit — stable runners returning after long breaks are worth monitoring in the market for any significant support.
Barmyblade (Tim Easterby, T14: 16/99) represents the highest-volume yard in the race — stable momentum is at its peak and despite the style compromise, any market move should be respected.

Mister Sky Blue and Bishop's Glory are the two prominent horses capable of slipping into the ideal tactical position behind Mrs Trump — their early positioning in the first two furlongs will be a decisive indicator of how the race unfolds.

races.name: David Lever Memorial Handicap

runners_data.name: Celtic Arrow
runners_data.note: Lightly raced 3yo from Julie Camacho with a form string of 3-4-2 over 5-6f on Standard ground; 112 days off is a query, and she is unproven on Good to Firm, but her style is genuinely unclassified (U) so her placement in the race is open.
runners_data.comment: Returning from a break of over three months, she shaped with promise as runner-up in her latest maiden; acts at 5-6f and bred to get further, with scope for improvement stepping into handicap company on turf, though the lengthy layoff requires some caution.

runners_data.name: Masai Angel
runners_data.note: Richard & David Fahey have hit a decent recent strike rate (5/56 over 14 days) and this 3yo has placed on Good going, but she is a true hold-up horse who will likely be pushed closer to the pace than she wants in this shape, blunting her natural finishing kick.
runners_data.comment: Third in his latest maiden at Ripon, beaten 6½ lengths, and without a win in his last three starts; effective at 6f and may benefit from the switch to handicap company, but our figures rank him towards the foot of the field for now.

runners_data.name: Country Artiste
runners_data.note: Form reads 55-670 and her last six runs include a string of mid-pack finishes; though her hold-up style suits waiting races, the race shape here will force her forward of her preferred position, and Good to Firm sim-going figures of 6/10 with no wins are uninspiring.
runners_data.comment: Failed to show her best at Ripon most recently, finishing well down the field, and without a win in her last five starts; effective at 6f on a sound surface and her handicap mark has been nudged downward, but she needs to find more to feature here.

runners_data.name: Hares Bredth
runners_data.note: Won last time over 6f on Good at this track (LR: 11 days), making her the freshest course-and-distance winner in the field; despite being a genuine hold-up horse displaced toward midfield, her proximity to winning form and Thirsk familiarity keep her relevant in a messy scenario.
runners_data.comment: Opened his account in a handicap at Redcar last time off a mark 5lb lower than today's, and while this represents a step up in class, he acts at 6f on good ground; first-time tongue-tie applied, and the task is to reproduce that recent effort at a higher mark.

runners_data.name: Concert
runners_data.note: Tom Marquand takes the ride on this Jack Channon 3yo who has placed on Good going but missed the frame in 13 runners last time; a genuine hold-up type who will be shuffled closer than ideal, and 43 days off plus a moderate sim-going record (4/9, 1W) tempers enthusiasm.
runners_data.comment: Finished a close third last time off a 1lb higher mark, and our figures give her the edge in this field; she acts well at 5-6f on good ground, a notable jockey appointment appeals, and first-time tongue-tie is applied. Modest yard form is the one caution.

runners_data.name: Liverpool Star
runners_data.note: Joanna Mason partners a horse who won over 6f on Good going and has place form in abundance (8/13 runs, 1W3P on sim-going); a hold-up type by style but races frequently and consistently, and her 6f Good win is directly relevant — the most compelling closer in the field if the pace is strong enough.
runners_data.comment: Proven at 5-6f on this going, he was well beaten when ridden patiently last time — a setup that clearly did not suit — and now drops a pound in the weights; his earlier form at this trip under more suitable conditions marks him as a genuine danger.

runners_data.name: Simba's Pride
runners_data.note: Michael Dods 3yo with an outstanding Good-ground record (8/8 runs, 2W3P) including wins over 6f; a prominent racer who can sit just behind Showtown and capitalise, and 15 days since last run suggests freshness without staleness — one of the key dangers in this race shape.
runners_data.comment: Fourth last time, making his strongest impression in the closing stages, and 1lb lower in the handicap today; effective at 5-6f on good ground and capable off this sort of mark, but our figures place him outside the leading group on this occasion.

runners_data.name: King's Road Dandy
runners_data.note: David Nolan partners a David & Nicola Barron 3yo whose recent form (3-5-8) is modest, and while he has placed on Good going, he is a true hold-up horse shuffled closer to the pace than suits; 40 days off and only three career runs over this trip limit confidence.
runners_data.comment: Second in our ratings and making his handicap debut following a well-beaten maiden run, the step into this sphere could unlock his potential; effective at 6f on good to firm and yet to score in recent starts, but capable of making his mark now conditions change.

runners_data.name: Showtown
runners_data.note: Kevin Ryan's 3yo is the lone confirmed front-runner and has placed on Good going (2/8 sim-going, 1P); the STYLE_FIT flag notes he is slightly out of role, but the absence of any serious pace rival means Tom Eaves should secure a soft lead and use the Good to Firm conditions to his advantage with a patient front-running ride.
runners_data.comment: First-time cheekpieces applied for a gelding who has placed but remains without a win in recent starts; he was held up for pace at this course last time but is effective over today's trip on good ground and rated close to his mark.

runners_data.name: Saucy Jane
runners_data.note: Sam James partners a Jack Morland 3yo who carries top weight (135lbs) and has a mixed sim-going record (7/14, 1W4P); a hold-up type by natural style despite the headgear (p) suggesting a forward move is possible, and her 2nd over 6f Good last time shows she can compete at this level.
runners_data.comment: Shaped as though the soft ground at Chester last time blunted her effort, and today's firmer surface is more to her liking; she acts well at 5-6f and first-time cheekpieces add interest, though she remains yet to score in recent starts.

runners_data.name: Go Lockers Go
runners_data.note: Daniel Tudhope on Michael Bell's consistent 3yo who has won twice on Good going and placed over 6f on Standard; a confirmed hold-up type wearing hood (hg:h) who is at his best when produced late — his Good-ground form (4/8, 1W3P) is the best strike rate among the closers, and Tudhope's experience is a live asset.
runners_data.comment: Two wins in his last five starts and runner-up on each of his last two outings, he continues in good heart; effective at 5-6f on a sound surface, 1lb above his last winning mark here, and a first-time hood could sharpen his effort further.

runners_data.name: Houndhill
runners_data.note: Nigel Tinkler's 3yo has a messy form profile (2-6-8-1-0) but that 5f win on Standard is notable and his prominent style means he will be one of the first to chase Showtown; visor (v) suggests keenness may need managing, and Good sim-going (4/9, 0W1P) flags he has not yet translated his style advantage into a win on this surface.
runners_data.comment: Dropped further down the field than usual last time — though with some mitigation — and a positive response is required; rated 1lb lower than that run, effective at the trip on good to firm, and a first-time visor could help.

races.paceDynamic: Showtown is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 12-runner 6f handicap on Good to Firm ground at Thirsk, and with no genuine rival likely to press for the lead from the off, Tom Eaves should be able to dictate a controlled, measured gallop from stall to home turn. Simba's Pride and Houndhill are the only other prominent types and will likely track Showtown in second and third, meaning the pace is set by one horse with a small group immediately on its shoulder rather than a contested burn. The field is heavily populated with hold-up horses — Masai Angel, Country Artiste, Hares Bredth, King's Road Dandy, Concert, Liverpool Star, and Go Lockers Go all have hold-up profiles but most will be forced closer to the pace than they naturally want to be, compromising their true finishing kick. This race shape — an uncontested leader setting a sustainable pace — classically favours horses racing prominently who can quicken from just off the shoulder, rather than genuine closers asked to deliver from farther back than ideal; prominent-to-pace profiles hold the clearest tactical edge here.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Showtown Leads, Holds On
scenarios.trigger: If Showtown dictates an uncontested, honest-but-not-scorching gallop and the field fails to produce a sustained late challenge.
scenarios.body: If Showtown dictates an uncontested, honest-but-not-scorching gallop and the field fails to produce a sustained late challenge.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Pinch It
scenarios.trigger: If Simba's Pride or Houndhill track Showtown closely enough to pounce as the leader ties up inside the final furlong.
scenarios.body: If Simba's Pride or Houndhill track Showtown closely enough to pounce as the leader ties up inside the final furlong.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late Closers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If Showtown sets a stronger gallop than expected and the pace-run tempo opens the door for hold-up horses to reel in the field.
scenarios.body: If Showtown sets a stronger gallop than expected and the pace-run tempo opens the door for hold-up horses to reel in the field.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos — No Shape Holds
scenarios.trigger: If there is a slow start, traffic trouble through the pack, or an unexpected challenger forces a contested early pace.
scenarios.body: If there is a slow start, traffic trouble through the pack, or an unexpected challenger forces a contested early pace.

watchPoints.text: Simba's Pride has an exceptional 8/8 Good-ground record including two wins over this trip — watch whether Mark Winn slots him directly onto Showtown's quarters, as that prominent position is the most dangerous attacking slot in this shape.

Go Lockers Go is the most credible closer in the field given Daniel Tudhope's experience and two Good-ground wins, but he needs Showtown to set a genuinely testing gallop — watch the early pace fractions; if it is a dawdle, his hold-up style is neutralised.

Showtown carries a STYLE_FIT flag suggesting he is slightly out of his natural role, and his sim-going record is thin (2/8, 0W1P on Good) — if he fails to dominate the early stages or is headed approaching the final furlong, his chance evaporates quickly.

Multiple hold-up horses (Masai Angel, Country Artiste, King's Road Dandy, Hares Bredth) are all running closer than they naturally want — watch for a congested midfield group that may cause interference or interference claims in a tight finish, particularly from the two-furlong pole onwards.

Hares Bredth won over this exact course and distance 11 days ago on Good going — the shortest turnaround in the field; watch whether Tim Easterby's pace pattern from that win is repeated, as any step forward in condition could make her unexpectedly competitive despite her displaced race position.

runners_data.name: Asia Force
runners_data.comment: A rangy sort built for staying trips who showed his level when six lengths third at Chester most recently — a course unlikely to play to his strengths — and he steps up to twelve furlongs here, a trip that should suit him much better. Yet to score in recent starts, but the distance switch is a clear plus.

runners_data.name: York Tower
runners_data.comment: Caught the eye with a staying finish over ten furlongs at Epsom on handicap debut, beaten five and a half lengths into fourth — his late surge suggested this step up to twelve furlongs will bring more. Tops our figures in this field, backed by a trainer operating at near 30% over the past fortnight.

runners_data.name: Yafreh
runners_data.comment: Second at Hamilton on his most recent start, beaten four lengths in a maiden over today's trip, he handles the distance and ground and has scope for progress on his handicap debut. The main question is whether he settles well enough to deliver that potential.

runners_data.name: Temple
runners_data.comment: Third on his handicap debut at Newmarket most recently, beaten two lengths off a mark 1lb above today's — a solid introduction suggesting his mark is workable. Effective at this trip and beyond on suitable ground, he has more to offer now he's finding his feet in handicap company.

runners_data.name: Parisian Scholar
runners_data.comment: Fourth in a visor at Lingfield most recently and never a threat there, he tackles today's trip back on turf where he needs to show considerably more. He handles good to soft and stays the distance, but trails the main market on our figures.

races.name: Weatherbys Global Stallions App Handicap

runners_data.name: Westmorian
runners_data.note: Seven-year-old who wants to race prominently and has done so throughout his career, but with so many forward types in this field he is unlikely to get his natural berth — his recent form reading of 90R-87 (including a refusal) is a red flag and he has not struck on similar going in 15 attempts.
runners_data.comment: Beaten five lengths at York last time in a form-line effort at the distance, he has the advantage of a slowly-easing mark and handles any conditions. A trainer in good nick is an encouragement, but his string of winless runs makes it hard to expect much more from him here.

runners_data.name: Bergerac
runners_data.note: Eight-year-old hold-up type wearing a hood; his record on good ground shows three placed efforts from nine but his form string of 400-00 suggests declining returns and he has been beaten well back in recent starts at this trip.
runners_data.comment: Down the field again in a handicap at York last time and in need of considerably better than of late, he tackles today's distance in first-time cheekpieces on a sound surface he handles. Connections have landed 2 of the last 5 runnings of this race, which is about the strongest case available on his current form.

runners_data.name: Juan Les Pins
runners_data.note: A genuine front-runner by instinct whose productive 6f form (1W4P from 8 comparable runs) is hard to ignore, but with the field loaded with prominent types he will be forced to race in a position that doesn't suit — his chance depends on whether the pace brings the race back to him late.
runners_data.comment: Free-running on his last start, he was caught close home but finished a creditable head second off a mark 2lb below today's. Two wins in recent starts confirm he's in competitive form, though the trainer's poor patch of late is worth noting.

runners_data.name: Mister Sox
runners_data.note: Tim Easterby runner who races prominently and has strong placed form at 6f on good ground (1W4P in 11 similar-going runs), but the redistribution problem pushes him off his natural pitch; quick turnaround of 10 days may suit a fresh type.
runners_data.comment: Third at Pontefract most recently, beaten a couple of lengths off the same official rating as today, he is competitively weighted at the distance on a sound surface. First-time cheekpieces add a gear-change angle, and connections took this race last year, though his overall profile leaves him below the key market players.

runners_data.name: Deep Havana
runners_data.note: NON-RUNNER — listed as the confirmed front-runner but does not take part; his absence removes the single anchor of the pace picture and is the defining tactical fact of this race.

runners_data.name: Strong Warrior
runners_data.note: True hold-up horse with 2W4P from 6 comparable runs on good ground; Warren Fentiman's 3lb claim is a practical asset and his recent third on good ground (3/6f/GOO) shows he retains ability at this level.
runners_data.comment: Third at Ripon on his recent return to turf — beaten four lengths off a mark 1lb above today's — he tops our figures with the highest rating in the field. Proven at six furlongs on a sound surface and coming fresh off that encouraging effort, he looks poised to deliver.

runners_data.name: Indian Run
runners_data.note: Hold-up type with 1W3P from 13 runs on good ground at this trip — consistent, if not prolific; Ryan Sexton takes the ride and Indian Run has finished second on his most recent start, suggesting he is in form heading into this contest.
runners_data.comment: Returning to form at Windsor most recently — narrowly denied by a neck off a mark 1lb below today's — he ranks second on our figures and looks set for a bold showing. Proven at the distance on a sound surface, there is every reason to think he can deliver on that promise.

runners_data.name: Lord Roxby
runners_data.note: Won at 6f on good ground at Thirsk in recent form and has a clean prominent racing style that makes him one of the more likely horses to actually secure a forward position; Alex Jary's 3lb claim is a bonus and course form is directly relevant.
runners_data.comment: Fourth off a mark of 84 last time on an unchanged handicap rating today, he ran to a consistent level at the distance on suitable ground. His figures leave him anchored at the foot of the main market, however, and he will likely need a performance above his recent ceiling to get involved at the sharp end.

runners_data.name: American Style
runners_data.note: Races prominently in his natural style but has not won in his last five starts on good ground (0W from 12 comparable runs despite 2 career wins on similar); squeezed into a midfield role by the sheer number of forward types, his recent form of 99-300 reads as a horse out of sorts.
runners_data.comment: Beaten well down the field in a handicap at Doncaster last time and finding little when asked, he is suited by the distance and handles any ground. A recovery from that below-par effort is needed, though connections have landed 2 of the last 5 runnings of this race.

runners_data.name: Veblen Good
runners_data.note: Won at 6f on good ground last time and Daniel Tudhope — one of the best northern jockeys — takes the ride; has the profile of a horse that can push forward and sustain it, with the OR of 89 giving him a realistic weight-for-age claim against the field.
runners_data.comment: A winner in recent starts and proven at the distance on this type of ground, he pairs with a sharp jockey-trainer combination from stall one. Off a pound lower than his poor last showing, he remains on a competitive mark and is capable of returning to form.

runners_data.name: Novello Lad
runners_data.note: Back-to-back winner at OR 89 with David Nolan aboard; 3W9P from 13 comparable runs on good ground makes him the standout form horse — races prominently and will look to bounce forward from stall one, which at Thirsk's straight 6f is a workable draw.
runners_data.comment: Back-to-back wins show he's in excellent nick at this distance, and he has the attitude to fight it out in a tight finish. Up 4lb for his recent success, there are questions about his effectiveness on softer ground and the trainer's poor recent form is a note of caution.

races.paceDynamic: Deep Havana is listed as the confirmed front-runner but is a non-runner, which fundamentally alters the pace picture — there is now no single dedicated pace-setter to anchor the lead, and the race devolves into a contested scramble among multiple prominent types. Westmorian, Juan Les Pins, Mister Sox, American Style, Lord Roxby, Veblen Good and Novello Lad all carry prominent-racing profiles, yet only two or three can realistically occupy those forward positions on a 6f track at Thirsk. This field holds considerably more front-running and prominent types than the race shape can accommodate: of those, Lord Roxby and Veblen Good — both proven at the trip on good ground — are best-placed to secure a genuine forward pitch, with Novello Lad also likely to press from the front having won his last two. The resulting contested early pace on fast ground at Thirsk favours hold-up horses or those with the tactical speed to come off a pressured front group in the final two furlongs, making strong-finishing hold-up types and those dropped into a genuine stalking position the most advantaged profile.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Contested Pace, Closers Strike
scenarios.trigger: If the surplus of prominent types creates a genuinely strong early pace that sets the race up for those coming from off it.
scenarios.body: If the surplus of prominent types creates a genuinely strong early pace that sets the race up for those coming from off it.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Pair Draw Clear
scenarios.trigger: If Lord Roxby and Veblen Good establish clean positions and the pace is honest but not truly strong, allowing them to control and quicken.
scenarios.body: If Lord Roxby and Veblen Good establish clean positions and the pace is honest but not truly strong, allowing them to control and quicken.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Novello Lad Dictates
scenarios.trigger: If Novello Lad, in form with back-to-back wins, pushes forward and finds an uncontested lead with the other prominent types settling behind.
scenarios.body: If Novello Lad, in form with back-to-back wins, pushes forward and finds an uncontested lead with the other prominent types settling behind.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Prominent Scramblers Collide
scenarios.trigger: If the early positional battle causes multiple horses to burn each other out, leaving an unusually chaotic race with no clean winner from any group.
scenarios.body: If the early positional battle causes multiple horses to burn each other out, leaving an unusually chaotic race with no clean winner from any group.

watchPoints.text: With Deep Havana a non-runner, watch the opening furlong closely — Novello Lad, Lord Roxby and Veblen Good are all likely to push forward simultaneously and whichever horse wins that positional battle will have a decisive tactical advantage.

Strong Warrior and Indian Run are the only genuine hold-up horses in the race; if the pace contest among the prominent types fails to materialise and the race is run at a moderate tempo, both are likely to find the winner too far gone by the time they hit their stride.

Westmorian's form includes a recent refusal (R in form string) — if he dwells at the start or causes interference in a field already crowded with early movers, he could disrupt the pace picture materially.

Going is officially Good To Firm at Thirsk across all races today despite the headline entry showing Good — horses with a form preference for fast ground (Novello Lad, Veblen Good, Juan Les Pins) receive a quiet boost, while any runner flagged with a going concern on softer surfaces should be monitored in market moves.

Three apprentice/conditional jockeys ride in this race (Fentiman 3lb, Jary 3lb, Kirrane) — in a contested early pace scenario, the combined weight allowances may become relevant in a tight finish, and errors of judgement in the positional battle early could cost their mounts dearly at 6f.

races.name: William Hill Summer Cup Saturday 1st August Book Now Handicap

runners_data.name: Tattie Bogle
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse trained by Charlie Johnston whose recent form reads well — a win and three places in the last five over 7f on Good, making this trip and going combination the sweet spot; Jason Hart's booking is positive and 8 days since last run is ideal freshness.
runners_data.comment: Took a handicap eight days ago by two lengths off a mark 5lb below today's, looking the dominant force; he handles this trip and ground well, and while the penalty stiffens the task, his form this season makes him a genuine threat.

runners_data.name: Farandaway
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner whose form is almost entirely over 5-6f on Southwell all-weather, so this 7f turf test on Good to Firm poses a genuine stamina and surface question; the sole pace-setter in the race, so it will dictate fractions, but its ability to see it out is the key doubt.
runners_data.comment: Returns from a break of close to three months off a mark that still looks very competitive — a length-and-a-quarter second at Southwell on today's exact rating backs that up — and he handles this trip and going well; he is our top pick and should go close.

runners_data.name: War Howl
runners_data.note: Hold-up type with a concerning fade flag and a grim recent form string of six consecutive low finishes; his history over 7f on Good going shows he has placed before but the current run of form offers little confidence.
runners_data.comment: Outpaced from a slow start at Wetherby last time and has been out of the frame consistently in recent outings; the mark is easing but there is significant improvement needed before he threatens here, and he sits near the foot of our ratings.

runners_data.name: Al Muqdad
runners_data.note: Wears headgear (p) and is trained by David O'Meara with only two similar-going wins in fifteen tries, though his last two runs on Good over 7f produced a second and a third — quietly consistent if not flashy; the five-day turnaround is very quick.
runners_data.comment: Narrowed the margin to a nose at Doncaster five days ago on today's exact mark, suggesting he's in good current form; the addition of first-time cheekpieces is an interesting stable trial, and he handles the trip and ground, though he has yet to get his head in front in recent starts.

runners_data.name: In A Hurry
runners_data.note: Another O'Meara hold-up runner, this one wearing a tongue-tie, who has placed in ten of twelve starts on comparable going — that strike rate is significant; Daniel Tudhope takes over in the saddle, which is a notable positive booking.
runners_data.comment: Showed a clear uptick at Catterick nine days ago, going down by just over a length off today's mark with a tongue-tie she retains; she's well suited by the trip and going, and with a strong jockey/trainer pairing at this track, she has every right to go one better.

runners_data.name: Avatar Jet
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up type by profile whose last three wins came over 8f, suggesting this 7f trip on fast ground may be a touch short; shown in midfield on the map because the field is overloaded with closers — his chance depends on a strong pace that doesn't materialise here.
runners_data.comment: Held his form at the same mark last time, finishing fourth by two and a quarter lengths in keeping with his recent profile; effective over today's distance, he remains on a rating that looks competitive at this level and could play a part.

runners_data.name: Vince Le Prince
runners_data.note: A natural hold-up performer mapped forward because the rear is too congested; has placed twice over 7f on Good going and Tim Easterby sends him here fit off a 20-day break, but the tongue-tie and soft-ground wins suggest Good to Firm may be sharper than ideal.
runners_data.comment: Third at Catterick three weeks ago off a mark a pound above today's; now equipped with tongue-tie and cheekpieces for the first time, which is a notable stable move, and he handles the trip on any ground, though he remains without a win in recent starts.

runners_data.name: Men Of Honour
runners_data.note: Ruth Carr's 4-year-old hold-up horse whose recent form is poor over 6f on Good ground; while his natural style is to come from off the pace, the lack of any win or place in current form and the step back to 7f make improvement hard to project.
runners_data.comment: Failed to land a blow from off the pace at Doncaster eleven days ago, beaten five lengths; the mark continues to ease but he has not offered enough in recent outings, and his trainer's strike rate of late is muted, adding to the concerns.

runners_data.name: King Of War
runners_data.note: Interesting hold-up type whose last five runs include a 7f Good win and two other placings at the trip — the form profile for this race fits better than his map position suggests; wore headgear (tp) and ran only yesterday, which is an obvious physical concern.
runners_data.comment: Took a handicap recently in taking fashion by over three lengths off a lower mark, confirming he's in the form of his life; today he adds tongue-tie and cheekpieces, his trainer is in good shape, and this trip and ground hold no fears.

runners_data.name: Way To Dubai
runners_data.note: Michael Appleby's 7-year-old hold-up horse mapped to midfield due to field congestion; has shown zero wins or places from fifteen starts on comparable going, making it very difficult to make a case regardless of race shape.
runners_data.comment: Caught short of racing room at his most recent outing on a shorter distance than today's ideal trip and was unable to get competitive; he handles the ground, but he has been out of the frame too often of late and has plenty to prove to feature here.

runners_data.name: Singoura
runners_data.note: Gemma Tutty's 4-year-old who has contested 7f on Good four times recently, placing twice — the track-and-trip profile is solid; Joanna Mason takes over, and 25 days since last run means she arrives reasonably fresh, though the trainer's 14-day strike rate is modest.
runners_data.comment: Struggled at Doncaster on her latest start, going down by five and a half lengths in what looks an uncharacteristic effort given the form she had shown beforehand; she handles this trip and going, and has a chance if she can produce something closer to her better level.

runners_data.name: We've Got This
runners_data.note: Legitimate prominent racer — one of only two non-hold-up types in the field — trained by Ivan Furtado whose recent wins came over 8f on Soft; stepping back to 7f on Good to Firm looks a quicker surface than preferred, but his prominent style means he may be involved in shaping the pace.
runners_data.comment: Fell below her best at Carlisle three weeks ago on ground that may have been softer than ideal; today's surface should suit better and she handles the trip, but she has struggled to reproduce her best form in recent outings and needs to find significantly more.

runners_data.name: Imperial Guard
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse from Michael Dods whose entire recent history is over 5-6f and his last eight runs show no win; the step up to 7f on fast turf is new territory and nothing in his profile suggests he is capable of picking up from the back in this company.
runners_data.comment: Raced too freely in a visor at this track last time, going down by five and a half lengths; he tends to show his best over shorter distances and his form over the past several months has been modest, leaving him with clear questions to answer.

runners_data.name: Rory's Gold
runners_data.note: Simon Waugh's 4-year-old hold-up type whose best form over 7f and 8f on Soft may mean this quicker Good to Firm surface blunts his finishing effort; apprentice Amie Waugh (3lb claim) takes the ride, and his zero placings from fifteen similar-going runs is a clear negative.
runners_data.comment: Placed at Ayr twelve days ago off a mark a pound below today's, going down by three-quarters of a length — encouraging form on paper; he can race freely at times and is our lowest-rated runner, making it difficult to see him reversing the figures.

races.paceDynamic: Farandaway is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 14-runner 7f handicap at Thirsk on Good to Firm ground, and with no genuine challenger for the lead, Oliver Stammers can dictate a controlled, uncontested gallop from the front. However, Farandaway's recent form has been almost exclusively over 5-6f at Southwell on the all-weather, meaning this extra furlong on turf represents a significant style and stamina query, and its STYLE_FIT flag (0.93) underlines it is already operating somewhat out of its optimal profile. We've Got This and Tattie Bogle offer the only other prominent or pace-pressing threats, but the reality is this field is overwhelmingly populated by hold-up horses — Avatar Jet, Vince Le Prince, Men Of Honour, King Of War, Way To Dubai, Singoura, Imperial Guard and Rory's Gold are all natural closers compressed into the midfield map position because they simply cannot all settle at the rear. The race shape therefore favours genuine hold-up horses with the acceleration to close on what is likely to be a steady-to-moderate pace set by a lone, potentially out-of-depth front-runner, with prominent racers who can sit just behind the leader and travel with cover holding a secondary positional advantage.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Farandaway Controls, Closers Chase
scenarios.trigger: If Farandaway bowls along unchallenged at a moderate gallop and the field settles into a processional shape before the home turn.
scenarios.body: If Farandaway bowls along unchallenged at a moderate gallop and the field settles into a processional shape before the home turn.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace Picks Up, Front Pair Clear
scenarios.trigger: If We've Got This or another prominent type presses Farandaway early and the tempo genuinely quickens, turning it into a test of stamina and tactical position.
scenarios.body: If We've Got This or another prominent type presses Farandaway early and the tempo genuinely quickens, turning it into a test of stamina and tactical position.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: True Closers Pounce Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is fast enough to string the field out and the hold-up horses find the gaps they need in the straight to deliver a late challenge.
scenarios.body: If the pace is fast enough to string the field out and the hold-up horses find the gaps they need in the straight to deliver a late challenge.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Messy Race, Winner From Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If the large 14-runner field breaks unevenly, several hold-up horses are forced wide or blocked, and the race fragments into multiple small groups.
scenarios.body: If the large 14-runner field breaks unevenly, several hold-up horses are forced wide or blocked, and the race fragments into multiple small groups.

watchPoints.text: Farandaway's stamina over 7f on turf is unproven — if it fades rapidly in the final furlong having set a slow pace, the hold-up horses may not have enough track left to finish properly, creating a vacuum that benefits whoever is closest.

King Of War ran only yesterday (1-day turnaround flagged) — monitor market moves and any late withdrawal news, as a horse running on consecutive days on quick ground is a significant physical risk and changes race shape if removed.

With 14 runners and virtually the entire field being natural hold-up types, traffic and positioning in the straight at Thirsk will be critical — watch for In A Hurry and Tattie Bogle securing a clean passage, as those who get blocked face an almost impossible task late.

David O'Meara runs two horses (Al Muqdad and In A Hurry) — trainer patterns and any stable confidence signals from the market are worth tracking, particularly given Tudhope's booking on In A Hurry suggests that may be the yard's first string.

The going report confirms Good to Firm for the 4:40, consistent with the rest of the card — no late softening expected, so any horse with a strong preference for cut in the ground (Vince Le Prince, Rory's Gold) faces a confirmed surface concern.
